title: Unit – 2 : Session – 11 : SLO – 2 | Interface Inheritance
sections: interface Animal { void eat(); }   // added missing semicolon/brace fix
interface Pet extends Animal { void play(); }
public void eat() { System.out.println("Cat is eating."); }
public void play() { System.out.println("Cat is playing."); }   // missing method added
public class TestPet { public static void main(String[] args){ Cat c = new Cat(); c.eat(); c.play(); } }
Output: Cat is eating. / Cat is playing.

Explanation: since Pet extends Animal, Pet inherits the eat() declaration; any class implementing Pet must implement BOTH eat() and play() — interface inheritance expands the contract the implementing class must fulfill.
